correctness.rationale: The two-column Gram reduction gives exact eigenvalues, determinant and inverse trace. Odd-order lower bound uses two unequal opposite-side chord pairings, monotone discrete chord-sum gaps and a sharp reverse-triangle equality classification. Independent exhaustive computation over 435897 four-subsets for 4≤N≤36 and exact formulas corroborates but does not replace proof. Risk: arithmetic/phase convention is covered by explicit displayed equations.

value.rationale: The natural problem fixes exactly four distinct equal-weight observations for two complex Fourier amplitudes on a finite digital grid. A complete all-order and optimizer classification quantifies when exact tightness is possible, and gives different sharp second-order eigenvalue versus fourth-order determinant/variance defects. These are motivated identifiable Fisher-information invariants, not arbitrary finite arithmetic examples. Generalizations to more modes or weighted samples remain open.
